title.quote: G RAPH T EXT: G RAPH R EASONING IN T EXT S PACE
title.value: GraphText: Graph Reasoning in Text Space

extractions.description: The paper proposes GRAPHTEXT, a framework that converts graph data into natural language via a graph-syntax tree, enabling LLMs (ChatGPT, GPT-4, Llama-2-7B) to perform node classification as text generation, in both training-free in-context learning and instruction-tuning settings, compared against GNN baselines on citation and webpage graphs.

type.quote: We conduct extensive experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of G RAPH T EXT.
type.justification: The paper proposes a framework and evaluates it empirically on benchmark datasets.

name.quote: LLMs have not made significant advancements in the realm of graph machine learning
name.justification: The paper advances graph machine learning via LLMs.

name.quote: Large Language Models (LLMs) have gained the ability to assimilate human knowledge and facilitate natural language interactions
name.justification: The work is on LLM/NLP methods (text space reasoning, prompting, instruction tuning).

name.quote: we demonstrate this capability on the node classification tasks
name.justification: Node classification is the evaluation task setting.

name.quote: G RAPH T EXT utilizes a single pre-trained LLM (ChatGPT) for all datasets without any graph-specific training.
name.justification: ChatGPT is used as the LLM backbone in GraphText.

is_executed.quote: We leverage G RAPH T EXT with ChatGPT and GPT-4 to perform graph reasoning on the provided example.
is_executed.justification: Queried via API for in-context learning experiments.

is_compared.quote: our best results from instruction tuning across various settings surpass those of ChatGPT and approach the GNN baselines
is_compared.justification: ChatGPT results compared against Llama-2 and GNNs.

execution_mode.quote: even without training on graph data, G RAPH T EXT with ChatGPT can deliver performance on par with, or even surpassing, supervised graph neural networks through in-context learning
execution_mode.justification: Used only for inference / in-context learning.
